chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A slave of Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) asked him for wealth, so he said: 'My share will come out, and I will share it with you.' He said, 'I am not content,' and he went to Muawiya, who gave it to him. So he wrote to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) informing him of what he had obtained from the wealth.

So Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) wrote to him: 'As for after, that which is in your hand from the wealth, there used to be an owner for it before you, and it will go to its owner after you. And what is for you from it is what you pave the way for yourself. So prefer yourself over the rectification of your children, for you are gathering for one of two men: either a man who works in it with the obedience of Allah, so he is fortunate with what you were unfortunate for, or a man who works in it with the disobedience of Allah, so he is unfortunate with what you gathered for him. And neither of these two is deserving that you prefer him over yourself and place a burden on your back.'
So hope for what has passed for the mercy of Allah, and trust for what remains for the sustenance of Allah.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic perspective on prioritizing personal spiritual preparation versus accumulating wealth for children?
ai.summary: This epistle from Imam Ali (AS) to a slave of Muawiya illustrates the Shia concept of *al-mal al-mubad* (wealth acquired through labor or grant) versus inherited wealth, emphasizing that the owner's spiritual state is the primary determinant of the wealth's benefit. The Imam advises prioritizing one's own *sa'ada* (happiness/success) in the Hereafter over the uncertain utility of wealth for offspring, reflecting the theological principle that sustenance (*rizq*) is divinely guaranteed. This narrative underscores the practical application of trusting in God's provision (*tawakkul*) while avoiding the spiritual burden of accumulating wealth for those who may not utilize it for obedience.

en.hubeali: H 14476 – Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from one of his companions, who has said:

Abu Abdullahasws has reported that ‘A slave of Amir-ul-Momineenasws asked himasws for some wealth, so heasws said: ‘When myasws share comes to measws Iasws will distribute it to you’. He said, ‘I am not content’, and he went to Muawiya who gave it to him. So he wrote to Amir-ul-Momineenasws informing himasws of what he had received from the wealth.

So Amir-ul-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> wrote to him: ‘Thereafter, that which is in your hand from the wealth, there used to be an owner for it before you, and it will get transferred to its (next) owner after you, but what is for you from it is what you pave the way for yourself (for the Hereafter). So prefer yourself over the correction of your children, for what you have gathered is for one of the two men - for a man who works in it by the obedience to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> so he is fortunate with what he receives from you, and as for a man who works in it by the disobedience to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> so he is unfortunate by what you have gathered for him, and there is none from these two who is deserving of being preferred over yourself, and do not place a burden upon your back.

So be hopeful of the Mercy of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> for what has past, and place your trust in the sustenance from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> for what remains (of your life)’.
